meta.title: N-API Go html-to-markdown
meta.body_summary: Replace unstable koffi FFI HTML-to-Markdown with a new N-API Go module, adding a hybrid N-API → koffi → JavaScript fallback and integrating N-API build into Docker and CI, to eliminate panics and improve performance.

perf_labels.notes: Claude_Code added cross‑language N‑API module with hybrid fallback; cubic bot flagged 8 non‑blocking safety/logging issues; PR converted to draft by author and never merged.

change_scale_vs_repository.interpretation: At 1840 changed lines across 26 files, this is a large‑scale change adding a complete native module with build, CI, and fallback infrastructure. The PR was closed as draft without merge, which is unusual for a claimed performance improvement and suggests incomplete work or lack of maintainer buy‑in after the initial bot review.

review_details.concern_detail: 8 non‑blocking suggestions from cubic‑dev‑ai bot covering concurrency race, unsafe C string handling, goroutine leak, supply‑chain checksum missing, logging format, and path robustness.
review_details.performance_claim: Direct C++ interface eliminates FFI overhead for faster HTML‑to‑Markdown conversion.
review_details.rejection_signals: PR converted to draft by author after bot review, no further activity; never merged.

capability_boundary.boundary_notes: Claude_Code attempted a multi‑language N‑API module with Go/C++/TypeScript integration, but the PR remained draft; the bot review flagged many correctness and safety gaps, suggesting the agent may have struggled to ensure robust native‑module loading and error handling across the stack.

detection_detail.code_reading: cubic‑dev‑ai bot performed static analysis on all new files, identifying issues related to concurrency, error handling, logging, and Docker supply‑chain security; no human maintainer review was recorded.

maintainer_practices.reproducibility_notes: No before/after performance data or benchmarks; the only evidence is the narrative claim of ‘no FFI overhead’.
maintainer_practices.regression_detail: The author converted the PR to draft shortly after the bot review and did not apply any fixes; it was never merged.

core_change_summary.description: Introduced a new N‑API Go module (go‑html‑to‑md‑napi) with a C++ wrapper and TypeScript loaders that implement a hybrid fallback (N‑API → koffi → JavaScript turndown). Added a multi‑stage Docker Go build stage, CI steps, and a validation script, and integrated the new module into the existing html‑to‑markdown.ts.

evidence.secondary_note: Build and CI updates ensure the native module can be compiled in Docker and tested; the legacy html‑to‑markdown.ts is kept as a fallback.
change_trajectory: Reverted previous koffi mutex fix to replace with N‑API.
Added full N‑API module with Go library, C++ wrapper, and TypeScript loaders.
Added CI build steps for N‑API compilation.
PR converted to draft by author after cubic‑dev‑ai bot review.

review_signals.summary: Dynamic data interpolated in log message instead of using structured context object.
Concurrent requests may receive a false negative because the guard returns napiModule before the asynchronous load completes.
Unprotected require of the native addon will throw at runtime and breaks the documented fallback mechanism.
Only the error message is logged, discarding stack and metadata; pass the original Error object instead.
Building the N‑API path with process.cwd() can fail if the service is started from a different folder; use __dirname instead.
The goroutine performing conversion is not cancelled when the context times out, causing a potential goroutine leak.
C.GoString is called without a NULL check; passing a null C string will crash the process.
The downloaded Go toolchain archive is used without verifying its checksum or signature.
Formal COMMENTED review linking to cubic.dev; 8 issues found across 20 files.

collaboration_trajectory: PR opened by mogery (co‑authored by Claude) with a large new N‑API module and hybrid fallback.
cubic‑dev‑ai bot posted 8 non‑blocking inline suggestions within minutes, covering safety, concurrency, and build security.
Author converted the PR to draft shortly after the bot review, and no further commits or review activity followed.
